idee_recherchee.texte: Time passes more slowly for an astronaut orbiting Earth or for a clock near a massive object than for someone far from gravity, an effect called time dilation that has been measured with atomic clocks and must be corrected in GPS satellites.

titre_video: Scientists Are Freaking Out Over Space Time (It's Not Real)
titre: L'holographie explique l'action fantomatique et l'illusion du temps
resume: On a flat 2D screen, entangled particles are not really far apart, so spooky action at a distance needs no magical communication. The same logic suggests that time as past, present and future is an illusion produced by our brains misreading quantum data.
texte: The holographic principle actually explains Einstein's spooky action at a distance idea well. If the two particles are entangled on a flat 2D screen, they're not actually communicating with one another in some magical mysterious way across light-years of 3D space. We just perceive them as being far apart, but in reality, they aren't. That same sort of logic can also be applied to time. We experience it in a linear sequential format, past, present, and future, but that too might just be an illusion. It's our brain's desperate attempt to interpret complex quantum data unfolding on a flat plane that we're hardwired to misunderstand.
